Alright so I spent a bunch more time on this finally.

First, there was a new issue related to open FD limits as discussed on the ML a few weeks back. It's really annoying that upstream docker image providers made this change, but I can sort of understand it.

I wish however that HAProxy put an upper cap on FD tab size by default, even after reading your arguments against more defaults. Because the number of systems capable of running HAProxy in situations where it actually *needs* 1 billion file descriptors is tiny. Probably even zero. Even with well-tuned network stacks, amazing NIC offloading, etc., I'm not sure it is even possible on current commodity hardware.

> CI may be executing the CI jobs with PID 1

I don't see how this is possible. First, pid 1 cannot have a session and always needs to be forked to do anything as simple as just getting Ctrl-C from a terminal, so I strongly doubt that any container solution continues to assign pid 1 to random processes (at least by default). Try to ctrl-C any shell started as "init=/bin/sh" to get a not-so-nice experience of what happens when trying to recover a system. Second, there's make, which itself forks vtest, which itself forks haproxy, none of the 3 being able to get pid 1 nor even the same pid between each other since fork() never creates pid 1, and all 3 processes must be running in parallel.

So on this case I'm fairly confident it's impossible for haproxy to be assigned pid 1. There could be plenty of other reasons for the signal not working though. But that remains a separate issue from the root cause here. What really happens is that the timeout triggers because the master doesn't seem to see the worker finishing, so it's waiting and doesn't quit.

         -> haproxy worker process: PID Z (receives forwarded SIGINT from tini init system)
